title: Unexpected kernel routing performance delta: incident follow-up and action items
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Summary:
During a routine scheduler tuning deploy (change set: scheduler v2.14 heuristics), we observed a 20–45% increase in P95 token-generation latency for small-batch chat workloads using Llama-2-13B-quant variants. The spike lasted ~4 hours on 2026-03-10 and affected ~12% of hosted API requests for affected customers (majority chat/low-batch).

Immediate impact and mitigation taken during incident:
- Detection: latency alert from SLO monitoring at 13:12 UTC; automated runbook executed. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/runtime/latency-2026-03-10
- Short-term mitigation: rolled back scheduler change to previous canary at 13:40 UTC which restored baseline within one request window.
- Customer comms: PG sent initial incident update to impacted customers and status page was updated.
- Hotfix: temporarily pinned small-batch routing rule to use legacy kernel selector for quant variants. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5123

Root cause (technical analysis):
- The scheduler change introduced a new cost model that slightly over-weighted cost-per-batch vs. cost-per-token for tiny batch sizes (1-4).
- As a result the kernel-selection heuristic started preferring a quantized kernel that performs well at larger batches but has high absolute per-token overhead for short sequences (chat single-turn <32 tokens).
- Interaction with auto-batching window caused some requests to miss prefix cache reuse, amplifying the per-request overhead.
- Regression surfaced only on quantized Llama-2 variants where fused attention kernel trade-offs differ from FP16.
- Contributing factor: incomplete unit coverage in the scheduler e2e perf tests for low-batch/short-seq distributions.

What went well:
- Alerting and rollback path worked; SLOs returned to baseline after rollback.
- Canary and feature-flagging allowed safe revert without infra churn.
- Post-incident blameless RCA completed within 48 hours and shared with customers.

Action items (owners and ETA):
1) Add fine-grained microbenchmarks for small-batch/short-sequence kernels (owner: Mei Tan, estimate: 3). ETA: 2026-03-21. Details: expand bench harness to include batch sizes 1–8 and sequence lengths 8,16,32; run across fp16/quant kernels and record per-token cold and warm latencies.
2) Implement explicit scheduler rule to prefer low-setup-overhead kernels for latenciesensitive routes (owner: Jacob Reynolds, estimate: 5). ETA: 2026-03-28. Implementation: new policy with threshold heuristics; include unit tests and canary.
3) Improve observability: instrument kernel-selection decisions in trace spans and expose per-request selection reason in Console traces (owner: Sofia Chen, estimate: 3). ETA: 2026-03-18. Links: Console tracing RFC in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RT/Kernel+Selection+Tracing
4) E2E regression test: add a nightly job that replays representative small-batch chat traffic against canaries after any scheduler change (owner: Backend CI team, estimate: 5). ETA: 2026-03-24. Artifact: replay harness in GH Actions workflow runtime/perf/replay.yml
5) Kernel selector safety net: add a lightweight runtime fallback that triggers when measured P95 increases >10% relative to baseline for 30m and automatically flips routing to legacy selector (owner: Runtime SRE, estimate: 8). ETA: 2026-04-04.
6) Review quantization kernel trade-offs and document guidance for model onboarding (owner: Applied ML - Mateo Alvarez, estimate: 3). ETA: 2026-03-25. Deliverable: internal playbook and model-variant matrix.
7) Post-release canary policy: require perf-replay pass for scheduler and kernel selector changes before pushing to 50% canary (owner: Product - Rachel Kim, estimate: 2). ETA: 2026-03-20.

Progress updates and checkpoints:
- 2026-03-11: Bench harness prototype completed (Mei Tan). Initial microbench shows quant kernel 3x higher cold setup for seq<=16.
- 2026-03-12: Emergency pin implemented and merged (PR #5123). Canary removed.
- 2026-03-13: Tracing RFC reviewed by Observability team; PR for trace spans opened (PR #5138).
- 2026-03-14: Scheduler rule design doc approved by runtime leads; implementation in progress (branch: feat/sched-low-overhead).

Review feedback and open decisions:
- PM asks whether user-facing rate limits or routing-by-tier should also be adjusted to proactively protect latency-sensitive customers. Decision: defer to a follow-up (ENG-21478) to evaluate product-level mitigations.
- Engineering lead requested a quant-kernel tuning experiment before changing the selector permanently — scheduled as part of action 6.

Related artifacts and links:
- Incident timeline and raw logs: https://incidents.redwood.ai/INC-2026-03-10-42
- Postmortem doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/postmortems/2026-03-10-kernel-routing-delta
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls?q=is%3Apr+5123+OR+5138
- Perf dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/runtime/latency-2026-03-10

Acceptance criteria for this ticket (all must be complete):
- Microbench suite added and passing in CI with historical baseline kept.
- Scheduler rule merged and canaried; perf replay passes on canary.
- Kernel-selection traces visible in Console for at least 14 days of retention in staging.
- Automatic fallback implemented and tested in a staging soak run.
- Playbook for model onboarding updated with kernel trade-offs.

Post-closure follow-ups (to be tracked separately):
- Customer retrospective sessions for top 3 impacted accounts (owner: Customer Success).
- Evaluate longer-term: scheduled work to explore new fused attention kernels and auto-tune thresholds (will spawn a dedicated RFC).

Notes and context for reviewers:
This ticket contains a mix of engineering fixes, observability improvements, and process changes. Prioritize safety-net and tracing first to reduce blast radius for future scheduler experiments. If any blocker emerges (e.g., perf-replay instability), flag immediately and open temporary rollback shields.

Comments:
- 2026-03-11 (Mei Tan): "Microbench shows the quant kernel's setup cost dominates for seq<20; adding warm-up caching reduces but does not fully close gap."
- 2026-03-12 (Jacob Reynolds): "Pinned legacy selector for small-batch routes; we should avoid broad pins — aim for targeted rule and test coverage."
- 2026-03-14 (Priya Nair): "Please attach the CI job link and note when the canary passes so I can update customer comms."

Files and artifacts to attach in ticket comments: runtime-perf-bench-results-20260311.csv, scheduler-change-diff.patch, perf-replay-workflow.yml
